tasks.title: API test CPU budget reflects current main measurements and passes branch confirmation
tasks.spec: ## Repository: api, Task, Checks 1-5 and Completion evidence; Required behavior 1-6 and the PR handoff of Required behavior 7; Counterexamples and Security impact. Keep all measurement and calculation stages in this single task. Follow the specified needs-input holds for unexpected precision, an already-reset main budget, or a failing pre-merge confirmation. Post-merge execution belongs to lorenzh, not task completion.

acceptance.expected: Exit 0. Required behavior 1: record the full current main SHA M once at task start and retain it for every measurement, including replacements. Obtain three counted measurement runs using a=b=M and others=main with the next command, one run at a time. Two are acceptable only if the third cannot complete and the PR explains why. Never dispatch three runs back to back or change the workflow's concurrency settings.

acceptance.command:
set -e
while :; do active=$(gh run list -R lorenzh/pulse-api -w bench.yml --json databaseId,status -L 20 --jq '[.[] | select(.status != "completed")] | length'); [ "$active" = 0 ] && break; sleep 30; done
t0=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
gh workflow run bench.yml -R lorenzh/pulse-api --ref main -f a="$M" -f b="$M" -f others=main
RUN_ID=
for lookup in {1..12}; do
  matches=$(gh run list -R lorenzh/pulse-api -w bench.yml -e workflow_dispatch -b main --json databaseId,createdAt -L 10 --jq "[.[] | select(.createdAt >= \"$t0\")]")
  count=$(printf '%s' "$matches" | jq length)
  if [ "$count" -gt 1 ]; then printf 'needs-input: ambiguous dispatch ids %s\n' "$matches"; exit 1; fi
  if [ "$count" = 1 ]; then RUN_ID=$(printf '%s' "$matches" | jq -r '.[0].databaseId'); break; fi
  sleep 5
done
[ -n "$RUN_ID" ] || { printf 'Run lookup failed; investigate before another dispatch\n'; exit 1; }
printf 'Measurement run id: %s; t0: %s\n' "$RUN_ID" "$t0"
while :; do status=$(gh run view "$RUN_ID" -R lorenzh/pulse-api --json status --jq .status); [ "$status" = completed ] && break; sleep 30; done
gh run view "$RUN_ID" -R lorenzh/pulse-api --json status,conclusion,event,headBranch
acceptance.expected: Required behavior 1 and Check 3: execute this single-dispatch procedure separately for each measurement and any replacement. The idle query prints 0 before dispatch, preventing cancellation of a pending nightly. Record t0 and the unique run id before waiting; more than one matching run requires needs-input with the ids, never a guess. The recorded run reaches completed before another dispatch; do not use gh run watch --exit-status as a success test. Retain the distinct ids and timing evidence in task/PR evidence. Only completed, non-cancelled runs with harness exit 0 or 1 and bench-out/table.json count; inspect/download with the next check before counting. Replace cancelled runs and harness exit 2 using this same idle/dispatch/identify/wait procedure. A gating failure conclusion is allowed. Do not count the separate confirmation run.

acceptance.command: gh run view "$RUN_ID" -R lorenzh/pulse-api --json status,conclusion,event,headBranch,headSha,jobs; gh run view "$RUN_ID" -R lorenzh/pulse-api --log; gh run download "$RUN_ID" -R lorenzh/pulse-api -n bench-out --dir "$RUN_DIR"; test -f "$RUN_DIR/table.json"; test -f "$RUN_DIR/samples.json"
acceptance.expected: Repeat for each counted measurement run with a distinct RUN_DIR outside the repository. Check 3 requires status completed, conclusion other than cancelled, event workflow_dispatch and headBranch main (literal expected values). Logs prove harness exit 0 or 1 and others=main. Download and both file checks exit 0. Exactly three distinct run ids are counted, or two with the PR's stated reason that the third cannot complete; no cancelled run is cited as a measurement. A workflow failure caused by budget or regression rows is allowed and its failing rows are retained for the PR.

acceptance.command: jq -c '.[] | select(.service=="api" and .metric=="test_cpu_s") | {a,b}' "$RUN_DIR/table.json"; jq -e --arg M "$M" '.refs.a.api == $M and .refs.b.api == $M and ([.refs.a, .refs.b][] | del(.api) | all(.[]; . == "main"))' "$RUN_DIR/samples.json"
acceptance.expected: Repeat for every counted measurement run. One api test_cpu_s row provides full-precision A and B medians from table.json, never table.md; the refs check exits 0 and prints true. The SHA comes independently from the main lookup in Required behavior 1.

acceptance.command: bun -e 'import assert from "node:assert/strict"; const paths = JSON.parse(process.env.MEASUREMENT_TABLES); assert.ok(paths.length === 2 || paths.length === 3); let U = 0n; for (const path of paths) { const rows = (await Bun.file(path).json()).filter(r => r.service === "api" && r.metric === "test_cpu_s"); assert.equal(rows.length, 1); const b = rows[0].b; assert.ok(typeof b === "number" && Number.isFinite(b) && b >= 0); const u = Math.round(b * 1e6); assert.ok(Number.isSafeInteger(u) && Math.abs(b * 1e6 - u) < 1e-3, "needs-input: non-integer microseconds"); const value = BigInt(u); if (value > U) U = value; } const T = (11n * U + 999999n) / 1000000n; const expected = Number(T) / 10; console.log(JSON.stringify({microseconds: String(U), tenths: String(T), budget: expected})); assert.equal((await Bun.file("bench/budgets.json").json()).api.test_cpu_s.budget, expected);'
acceptance.expected: Exit 0. MEASUREMENT_TABLES is a JSON array of paths to the separate counted runs' downloaded table.json files. The independent expected budget is the highest B median times 1.10, rounded upward only at the end to 0.1 s using integer microseconds and BigInt, as in Required behavior 2 and Check 3. A precision failure requires needs-input. Preserve full precision in the README and PR; do not average runs or take the largest raw sample.

acceptance.command: bun -e 'import assert from "node:assert/strict"; const cases = [[7.000001,7.8],[9.090910,10.1],[7,7.7],[8.674321,9.6]]; for (const [b, expected] of cases) { const u = BigInt(Math.round(b * 1e6)); assert.equal(Number((11n * u + 999999n) / 1000000n) / 10, expected); } const invalid = 8.6743215 * 1e6; assert.ok(Math.abs(invalid - Math.round(invalid)) >= 1e-3);'
acceptance.expected: Exit 0; the spec's literal precision counterexamples yield 7.8, 10.1, 7.7 and 9.6 s respectively, and 8.6743215 s fails the whole-microsecond check. Run this as an ephemeral calculation; add no test or calculation file to the repository.
Exit 0; repository lint, typecheck and full test suite including the coverage gate pass (Check 1).
Exit 0, matching the bench-selftest CI job described in Tool facts. The hosted measurement and confirmation runs supply the whole-stack bench evidence.

acceptance.command: diff <(git show "$B0:bench/budgets.json" | jq -S 'del(.api.test_cpu_s.budget)') <(git show "$H:bench/budgets.json" | jq -S 'del(.api.test_cpu_s.budget)'); git show "$B0:bench/budgets.json" | jq .api.test_cpu_s.budget; git diff --name-only "$B0" "$H"; git diff --check "$B0" "$H"; git diff "$B0" "$H" -- bench/budgets.json
acceptance.expected: Check 2: B0 is the recorded base main and H is the implementation head. The normalized diff is empty (exit 0), the old budget is the literal 5.6, the changed-path list is exactly bench/README.md and bench/budgets.json, and diff --check exits 0. The raw JSON diff changes only api.test_cpu_s.budget with Biome formatting. Floor 1.6, unit, gating, thresholds, baseline, other metrics, workflows, dependencies and product code remain unchanged. If main already reset the budget to at least the computed value, hold with needs-input per the repository section. These checks also substantiate Security impact: no.

Check 5 and Required behavior 4: only the api bullet of Temporary test floors changes. It preserves the floor's original derivation, 1.6 s and run ids 41508721559, 41517811504, 41525755478, 41578638886; records the former 5.6 s budget; cites the owner decision on meta #761 and every counted measurement run URL, M, others=main, full-precision B medians, maximum and exact calculation/result from those artifacts. It calls the budget temporary and an exception to the usual 30 percent rule. The introductory paragraph, notify/status bullets and closing release-tag paragraph stay unchanged.

acceptance.command:
set -e
git push -u origin "$TASK_BRANCH"
M1=$(gh api repos/lorenzh/pulse-api/commits/main --jq .sha)
[[ "$M1" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]
while :; do active=$(gh run list -R lorenzh/pulse-api -w bench.yml --json databaseId,status -L 20 --jq '[.[] | select(.status != "completed")] | length'); [ "$active" = 0 ] && break; sleep 30; done
t0=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
gh workflow run bench.yml -R lorenzh/pulse-api --ref "$TASK_BRANCH" -f a="$M1" -f b="$M1" -f others=main
CONFIRMATION_RUN_ID=
for lookup in {1..12}; do
  matches=$(gh run list -R lorenzh/pulse-api -w bench.yml -e workflow_dispatch -b "$TASK_BRANCH" --json databaseId,createdAt -L 10 --jq "[.[] | select(.createdAt >= \"$t0\")]")
  count=$(printf '%s' "$matches" | jq length)
  if [ "$count" -gt 1 ]; then printf 'needs-input: ambiguous dispatch ids %s\n' "$matches"; exit 1; fi
  if [ "$count" = 1 ]; then CONFIRMATION_RUN_ID=$(printf '%s' "$matches" | jq -r '.[0].databaseId'); break; fi
  sleep 5
done
[ -n "$CONFIRMATION_RUN_ID" ] || { printf 'Run lookup failed; investigate before another dispatch\n'; exit 1; }
printf 'Confirmation run id: %s; t0: %s\n' "$CONFIRMATION_RUN_ID" "$t0"
while :; do status=$(gh run view "$CONFIRMATION_RUN_ID" -R lorenzh/pulse-api --json status --jq .status); [ "$status" = completed ] && break; sleep 30; done
gh run view "$CONFIRMATION_RUN_ID" -R lorenzh/pulse-api --json status,conclusion,headBranch,headSha
acceptance.expected: Required behavior 6: after the last measurement completes, commit the two files, pass local checks and push the branch containing the computed budget. Record full main SHA M1, task branch and head H. The confirmation follows the same idle-group, timestamp, unique-id and completion procedure as measurements; ambiguous ids require needs-input. Its headSha must contain the new budget. Replace a cancelled confirmation with the same procedure; a harness error supplies no confirmation evidence. This separate run never contributes to the computed budget. Inspect its artifact with Check 4 next.

acceptance.command: gh run view "$CONFIRMATION_RUN_ID" -R lorenzh/pulse-api --json status,conclusion,headBranch,headSha,jobs; gh run download "$CONFIRMATION_RUN_ID" -R lorenzh/pulse-api -n bench-out --dir "$CONFIRMATION_DIR"; jq -e --argjson expected "$EXPECTED_BUDGET" '[.[] | select(.service=="api" and .metric=="test_cpu_s")] | length == 1 and (.[0] | .verdict == "ok" and .budget.budget == $expected)' "$CONFIRMATION_DIR/table.json"; jq -e --arg M1 "$M1" '.refs.a.api == $M1 and .refs.b.api == $M1 and ([.refs.a, .refs.b][] | del(.api) | all(.[]; . == "main"))' "$CONFIRMATION_DIR/samples.json"
acceptance.expected: Check 4: completed confirmation run has headBranch equal to TASK_BRANCH and headSha equal to H (or a later head with identical budgets.json). Both jq checks exit 0 and print true. EXPECTED_BUDGET is the independently computed value from the measurement artifacts, not from the edited file or confirmation artifact. The literal required verdict is ok; the numeric budget is nested at .budget.budget in the actual Row schema. Other failing rows may make the workflow fail. If the api test_cpu_s verdict is not ok, hold with needs-input and the row/M/M1; do not increase the budget again or widen the floor.

Required behavior 5 and Completion evidence: PR body follows option (B) of meta #761 and retains Closes lorenzh/pulse-meta#<child> with the actual child number. It cites each measurement run URL, full a/b SHA M, others=main, full-precision A/B medians, maximum B, exact calculation and result from the downloaded artifacts; explains any two-run exception; cites the separate confirmation URL, head SHA, M1 and its api test_cpu_s row; lists other failing rows as out of scope and reports local checks and unchanged gates/security scope. A Post-merge acceptance section explicitly assigns lorenzh, the person merging, to read M2 with gh api repos/lorenzh/pulse-api/commits/main --jq .sha after merge, then run gh workflow run bench.yml -R lorenzh/pulse-api --ref main -f a=<M2> -f b=<M2> -f others=main and post its URL/row on meta #761. Expected post-merge verdict is the literal ok; a failure becomes a new issue. This acceptance checks the written handoff only; task completion does not wait for merge or the owner's run.
